stimulus.text: The photograph, taken in September 1957, shows a student of the Little Rock Nine arriving at Central High School in Little Rock, Arkansas, escorted by soldiers of the 101st Airborne Division. Governor Orval Faubus had used the Arkansas National Guard to block nine Black students from entering the school. President Dwight D. Eisenhower then federalized the National Guard and sent about 1,000 paratroopers to enforce the federal court order. In the same month, Congress passed the Civil Rights Act of 1957, the first federal civil rights law since Reconstruction.

stem: The Civil Rights Act of 1957 is best described as which of the following?

options.text: A law that ended segregation in all public places at once
options.misconception: Background from the books: segregation in public places was not ended until the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

options.text: A law that gave the Commission power to order desegregation itself
options.misconception: Background from the books: the Commission could only investigate and report, not order desegregation.

options.text: A law that was never signed by the president at all
options.misconception: Background from the books: President Eisenhower signed the act on September 9, 1957.

options.text: A first step with weak enforcement, though it created new federal machinery

rationales.A: Background from the books: segregation in public places was not ended until the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the Commission could only investigate and report, not order desegregation.
rationales.C: Background from the books: President Eisenhower signed the act on September 9, 1957.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the act broke an eighty-year silence and built new federal machinery, yet Southern opposition had stripped its enforcement powers.
rationales.general:
1. The act was the first federal civil rights law since Reconstruction, so it broke a long silence.
2. Background from the books: it created a Civil Rights Commission and a Civil Rights Division in the Justice Department.
3. Background from the books: a record filibuster by Senator Strom Thurmond and Southern opposition watered the bill down, so Black voter registration barely moved.
4. A law that builds machinery but cannot enforce it is a first step, not a finish.
Remember: judge a first law by the machinery it builds and the power it lacks.
